sections.title:
Where AI research
meets venture creation.
sections.content_html:
We bring founders, researchers, investors and technology partners together to explore how AI changes the way businesses are built.

Through practical programmes and field research, the Lab helps entrepreneurs put AI to work in their ventures — and turns those experiences into evidence that others can use.

sections.title: Your questions, answered.
sections.content_html:
Who can apply?

Early-stage founders from anywhere in the world can apply. You must be at least 18. You do not need an INSEAD affiliation or an AI product.

Is the Sprint free?

Yes. There are no participation fees and the Lab takes no equity.

How much time should I set aside?

Plan for around 2–3 hours each week during onboarding and the final weeks, and 4–5 hours each week during the build phase. The Sprint does not require full-time availability.

When do applications close?

Applications close on 1 December 2026 at 11:59 pm Singapore time (GMT+8). Selected founders are expected to be notified in early January 2027.

Can I take part as a mentor or Community Lead?

Yes. The Lab welcomes mentors and Community Leads. Use the involvement links below to learn more and apply.

Weeks 1–2

Onboarding

Meet your peer group and get familiar with the core frameworks.

2–3 hours/week
02

Weeks 3–8

Build

Apply AI through study groups, masterclasses and mentor sessions.

4–5 hours/week
03

Week 9

VC Week

Hear investor perspectives and explore what makes a company investable.

2–3 hours/week
04

Week 10

Test and refine

Use mentor feedback to sharpen your work and prepare for Demo Day.

2–3 hours/week

Sessions are in English. Recordings are available when needed. Demo Days follow the Sprint; venues are to be announced.

sections.title:
Ambitious founders.
Any sector. Anywhere.
sections.content_html:
The Sprint welcomes early-stage founders, from ideation through venture execution. You do not need to be building an AI product or have an academic affiliation.

  • Age 18 or over
  • A clear problem and motivation to build
  • Ready to participate, experiment and learn with peers
